title: Storytelling
summary: We read three funny short stories and chose the best title for each one. We studied the three narrative tenses: past simple, past continuous and past perfect. Then we told our own stories and retold a partner's story to someone else.

grammar.title: Past simple and past continuous in stories
grammar.explain: We use the past simple for completed actions in the past, like the main events of a story. We use the past continuous for an action that was in progress at a time in the past. It often gives the background, and a past simple action interrupts it.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم الماضي البسيط للأفعال المكتملة في الماضي، مثل الأحداث الرئيسية في القصة. ونستخدم الماضي المستمر لفعل كان مستمراً في وقت ما في الماضي؛ وهو غالباً يصف خلفية القصة، ثم يقطعه حدث بالماضي البسيط.
form: Past simple: subject + past form (worked, hit, sank). Negative: didn't + base verb.
Past continuous: subject + was / were + verb-ing. Negative: wasn't / weren't + verb-ing.
Background + event: was / were + -ing ... when + past simple.

examples.en: A magician was working on a cruise ship.
examples.note: Past continuous: the background of the story.

examples.en: The ship hit an iceberg and sank in a few minutes.
examples.note: Past simple: the main events, one after another.

examples.en: A fishing boat was working off the coast of Japan when a cow fell from the sky.
examples.note: A long action (was working) is interrupted by a short one (fell).

examples.en: They were sitting in prison when a man came forward.

examples.note: Past simple negative: didn't + base verb.

mistakes.wrong: When I was living in London, I was buying a dog.
mistakes.right: When I was living in London, I bought a dog.
mistakes.why: Buying the dog is one completed event, so use the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: They didn't find a dress, so they go to the tailor.
mistakes.right: They didn't find a dress, so they went to the tailor.
mistakes.why: Keep the story in the past: went, not go.

mistakes.wrong: The magician performed when the ship hit an iceberg.
mistakes.right: The magician was performing when the ship hit an iceberg.
mistakes.why: The action in progress uses the past continuous.

quiz.q: The parrot ___ comments every evening while the magician was performing.
quiz.why: A completed, repeated action in the past: past simple.

quiz.q: They ___ over the sea near Japan at the time.
quiz.why: An action in progress at that time: past continuous.

quiz.q: I was walking home when it suddenly ___ to rain.
quiz.why: The short action that interrupts uses the past simple.
Negative past simple: didn't + base verb.

quiz.q: When I ___ in London, I bought a dog.
quiz.why: The background situation: past continuous (was living).

quiz.q: Which tense do we use for the main events of a story?
quiz.why: Completed main events use the past simple.

grammar.title: Past perfect
grammar.explain: We use the past perfect for a completed action that happened before another action or time in the past. It helps the listener understand which thing happened first.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم الماضي التام لفعل اكتمل قبل فعل آخر أو وقت آخر في الماضي. وهو يساعد المستمع على فهم أيّ الحدثين وقع أولاً.
form: had + past participle: had gone, had flown, had thrown
Often used with after, before, when, already, by the time

examples.en: After they had gone about ten miles, he noticed the sheep looked tired.
examples.note: First they drove ten miles, then he noticed.

examples.en: He hadn't noticed that the man had a sheep with him.
A few weeks before, they had flown a cow from Russia to South Korea.
examples.note: This happened before the man came forward.

examples.en: The magician had listened to the same thing every night for six months.
examples.note: Before the night the ship sank.

examples.en: After I had had him for about six months, I took him to a training school.

mistakes.wrong: After I had him for six months, I took him to school.
mistakes.right: After I had had him for six months, I took him to school.
mistakes.why: The past perfect of 'have' is 'had had'.

mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, the film already started.
mistakes.right: When I arrived, the film had already started.
mistakes.why: The film started first, so use the past perfect.

mistakes.wrong: I didn't owned a pet before I got Fred.
mistakes.right: I hadn't owned a pet before I got Fred.
mistakes.why: For an earlier past, use hadn't + past participle.

mistakes.wrong: He had run away before the police had came.
mistakes.right: He had run away before the police came.
mistakes.why: The later action uses the past simple, and the past participle of 'come' is 'come'.

quiz.q: After I ___ him for about six months, I took him to a training school.
quiz.why: The earlier action uses the past perfect: had + had.

quiz.q: I ___ a pet before I had Fred.
quiz.why: Before another past time: hadn't + past participle.

quiz.q: When the police arrived, the thief ___.
quiz.why: The escape happened first, so use the past perfect.

quiz.q: He ___ that the man had a sheep with him.
quiz.why: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle.

quiz.q: Which action happened first? 'When I got to the station, the train had left.'
quiz.why: The past perfect (had left) shows the earlier action.
